# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 37 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 37-38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 37

**1** His disciples said: "When will you be revealed to us and when will we see you?"

**2** Jesus said: "When you strip without being ashamed, take your garments, place them under your feet like little children, and trample on them —

**3** then you will see the Son of the Living One and you will not be afraid."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Strip without being ashamed"** — consensus. The shameless nudity directly echoes Gen 2:25 ("the man and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame"). The recovery of prelapsarian innocence is the condition of vision.

**"Trample on them"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "stomp." The trampling of the garments = active defeat of the garment-self; it is not casual.

**"Son of the Living One"** — consensus. This is the full Christological title in Thomas; "the Living One" is the divine Father (cf. Saying 3's "Living Father"). The vision of the Son is also a vision of the divine source.

**Connection to Saying 21:** Saying 21's children who strip their clothes and return them establishes the motif; Saying 37 is its eschatological culmination. The stripping is not humiliation but liberation.

**Synoptic Parallels:** No direct parallel. The eschatological revelation question ("when will we see you?") appears in different forms in John 14:8-9. The nudity-as-spiritual-condition is unique to Thomas.

**Theological Note:** The garments represent: (1) bodily shame (the Fall), (2) social identity, (3) the gendered, divided self. To strip them and trample them is to undo the Fall and recover the undivided image in which one can see the divine.
